title: Safety-anchored variant editor journey notes
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures UX notes, wireframe descriptions, operator journeys, and a prioritized backlog for a 'Safety-anchored Variant Editor' in the Rollouts console. The editor's core idea: when teams create or edit rollout variants (canary/A-B/traffic slices), they can attach safety probes and fallback policies inline, see simulated outcomes, and get explicit microcopy telling them when a variant is 'safety-anchored' vs 'speculative'.

Background / Why this exists:
- Operators repeatedly forget to attach guardrails when creating variants; incidents surface late.
- Current fallback wiring is in a separate flow — users must configure fallback in a different tab. That separation increases mistakes and deployment risk.
- We want a single surface where variant configuration, safety probes, and automatic fallback policies are authored and previewed together.

Problem statements:
- Too many clicks across tabs to associate canary metrics with fallback actions.
- Hard to reason about precedence when multiple fallbacks exist (model variant fallback vs region fallback vs capacity fallback).
- Lack of a clear preview/simulation leads to overcautious broad rollouts or under-protective canaries.

Goals (measurable):
- Reduce time-to-create-variant-with-guardrails by 40% (baseline from internal telemetry).
- Reduce post-rollout rollback incidents caused by missing fallback by 50% within 3 months of launch.
- Surface explicit safety state (OK / Warning / Unsafe) with recommended actions.

Primary personas:
- Platform Operator: configures rollouts on behalf of product teams; needs clarity and audit trail.
- Product PM: defines success metrics and wants a safe A/B experiment.
- SRE/Oncall: needs quick ability to stop or auto-roll back when safety thresholds breach.

High-level journey flows (operators):
1) Create variant -> define traffic % and model variant -> anchor safety probes (select existing probes or create quick probe inline) -> choose fallback policy (predefined or custom) -> run preview simulation -> save & start rollout.
2) Edit variant mid-rollout -> console warns if safety probe drift detected -> operator can update thresholds or toggle stricter fallback immediately.
3) Emergency stop -> single-click abort in variant header; system surfaces which safety probes fired and why fallback didn't trigger (if applicable).

Key UX surfaces and wireframe notes:
- Left column: Variant spec (name, description, model id, traffic target slider + numeric input, tags).
- Middle column: Safety anchor panel (probe picker, quick-probe creation, threshold inputs). Quick-probe creation is a condensed form: metric, aggregation, window, threshold, alert severity.
- Right column: Fallback composer (radio: immediate fallback / gradual stepdown / region-shift / model-fallback). Each option reveals parameters and a preview line chart.
- Top bar: safety state pill (green/yellow/red) + small tooltip explaining which probe determines state. Action buttons: Preview Simulation, Start Rollout, Save Draft.
- Preview modal: timeline simulation with synthetic traffic and metric traces, toggles to simulate noisy traffic, and an event list where fallback triggers would occur.

Microcopy examples (inline suggestions):
- Safety state pill: 'Safety: Anchored — 1 probe OK, 0 warnings' (hover -> 'Click to inspect probes and thresholds')
- Probe picker empty state: 'No probes attached. Attach a safety probe to enable automatic fallback. Recommended for all canaries.' + link 'Create quick probe'.
- Fallback composer header: 'When probe breaches, automatically:' followed by three option cards with short descriptions and estimated recovery time.
- Preview CTA: 'Simulate for 30s with current traffic profile'

Edge cases & interaction notes:
- Multiple probes conflict: if one probe is informative-only and another is blocking, state should be 'Warning' and tooltip should explain precedence.
- Chaining fallbacks: operator can choose primary fallback (model -> region -> capacity). Show explicit order and allow drag-reorder.
- Existing legacy rollouts: when editing older rollouts without attached probes, show a one-time guided onboarding callout.
- Permission gating: only show 'Start Rollout' if user has rollout.create and rollout.start permissions. Otherwise show 'Request approval' CTA.
- Autosaved drafts: draft names should include variant and timestamp; show 'Resume editing' in console home.

Simulation behavior (notes for backend/product):
- Simulation should use recent rolling-window metrics (last 24h) as baseline and allow synthetic delta +/- X%.
- For probes that depend on external signals (customer satisfaction), fallback simulation should surface 'data not available' state.
- Sim should produce an event timeline, not just a single verdict.

Observability & audit expectations:
- Every change to variant or attached fallback must record who/when/why (free text reason).
- The variant detail page should show historical probe fires and whether fallback executed, plus traces linking to logs.

Operator keyboard and accessibility flows:
- Keyboard: tab-through panels left->right, enter to open probe editor, space to toggle fallback options. Escape closes preview modal.
- Screen reader: safety pill should announce 'Safety anchored, one probe OK, fallback set to immediate model-fallback'. Ensure all form inputs have labels and help text.

Backlog (prioritized, with approximate estimates):
- RF-201: Inline quick-probe composer (MVP) — 3 days.
- RF-202: Fallback composer with 4 fallback types and drag-order UI — 5 days.
- RF-203: Preview simulation engine API & timeline rendering — 2 weeks.
- RF-204: Safety state pill + precedence rules + tooltip copy — 2 days.
- RF-205: Onboarding callout for legacy rollouts + migration guide — 3 days.
- RF-206: Audit trail UI on variant details + export to CSV — 4 days.
- RF-207: Permissions gating and request-approval flow — 4 days.
- RF-208: Accessibility pass & keyboard shortcuts — 2 days.

Notes on polish & future ideas (nice-to-have):
- Small visual indicator on Console home showing number of running variants with 'safety warnings'.
- Slack webhook quick-action: when a probe fires, allow operator to trigger abort from Slack message (with auth).
- ML-recommended thresholds: suggest thresholds based on historical variability of metrics.

Open questions to resolve in grooming session:
- Which probe types are considered blocking by default? (latency, error-rate, hallucination-rate?)
- Should the preview simulate cross-variant interference (shared cache / KV influence)?
- How to present costs impact of a fallback (e.g., switching to smaller model reduces cost but increases latency) — worth showing an estimated cost delta in the preview?

Short-term next steps (this sprint):
- Align on blocking probe list with SRE and Applied ML (owner: Samira) — action: quick 30-min sync.
- Product design: sketch two low-fidelity wireframes for 'Create variant' and 'Preview modal' (owner: Maya) — due in 3 days.
- Engineering: prototype quick-probe creation API contract and a mock simulation endpoint (owner: Ethan) — spike 4 days.

Appendix: quick sketches pointers (for designers):
- Use vertical cards for panels, allow collapsing to focus on one area.
- Safety pill should remain sticky as user scrolls.
- Preview modal should be exportable as PNG and attachable to rollout run for postmortems.

Draft notes / unpolished thoughts (notes-to-self):
- Think about 'speculative variant' label for experiments that intentionally run without guardrails (should be discouraged but supported for internal research teams).
- Consider a library of probe templates for common signals (latency p95, server error %, answer-quality-check fraction).
- If we support function/tool calling in models, probe definitions might need to be able to evaluate structured outputs (e.g., JSON schema mismatches).

-- end of notes --
